growth_story.headline: Mozambique's post-war boom ended with the 2016 hidden-debt scandal; conflict, shocks and debt strain have left income per person about where it was in 2014.
growth_story.arc: Mozambique's income per person grew only 1.5 percent a year in 1990–1997, a stretch that spans the last years of the civil war and the early peace. From 1998 to 2015 it grew 5.2 percent a year, one of the fastest runs in Africa, as peace allowed a long recovery. Growth broke in 2016, when hidden state borrowing came to light and outside financing dried up, and since then income per person has shrunk by 0.4 percent a year on average. Insurgency in the north from 2017, the storms of 2019 and the pandemic, when income per person fell 4.1 percent in 2020, deepened the slump. After the unrest that followed the October 2024 elections, income per person fell 3.3 percent in 2025. It peaked in 2018, is now 5.7 percent below that peak, and is about where it first was in 2014.

threads.title: Peace and a long catch-up
threads.text: The end of the civil war in 1992 opened two decades of fast growth, among the highest in the region. In the data, income per person climbs steadily from 1998 to 2015, at 5.2 percent a year.

citations.title: Mozambique Country Economic Memorandum: Mozambique Needs a New Growth Model for Sustained, Inclusive Development
citations.quote: Growth accelerated remarkably following the end of the civil war, averaging 7.9% between 1993 and 2015—among the highest in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA).

threads.title: Hidden debts come to light
threads.text: In 2016, large loans taken on in secret by state companies were revealed. Outside lending stopped, and the IMF dates the long slowdown from that shock, with weaker investment and productivity since. Debt strain still shapes the economy today.

citations.title: Growth Challenges and Policy Priorities in Mozambique (Selected Issues Paper SIP/2026/014)
citations.quote: In 2016, previously undisclosed debt that included borrowing of about US$1.4 billion by two SOEs (Proindicus and MAM) came to light.

citations.title: Republic of Mozambique: 2025 Article IV Consultation—Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Republic of Mozambique
citations.quote: Since the hidden debt scandal in 2016, growth performance has weakened (SIP), poverty rates have risen (Figure 2), and external financing has declined.

threads.title: Insurgency, storms and pandemic
threads.text: An insurgency in the north grew from 2017, cyclones struck in 2019 and the pandemic hit in 2020. Each deepened the slowdown that began with the debt crisis; income per person fell 4.1 percent in 2020.

citations.title: Mozambique Country Economic Memorandum: Mozambique Needs a New Growth Model for Sustained, Inclusive Development
citations.quote: The slowdown has been exacerbated by the natural disasters in 2019, the escalation of insurgency in Northern Mozambique since 2017, and the pandemic since 2020.

threads.title: Gas project paused, then restarted
threads.text: Insecurity in the north paused the onshore gas project in 2021, and the pause ended in October 2025. The World Bank expects gas construction to support a modest recovery. Growth has leaned on mining and gas, which create few jobs.

citations.title: Republic of Mozambique: 2025 Article IV Consultation—Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Republic of Mozambique

citations.title: Macro Poverty Outlook: Mozambique

threads.title: Unrest and money shortages
threads.text: Protests after the October 2024 elections cut output sharply, and the recovery since has been fragile. Shortages of foreign currency and strained public finances have held it back.

growth_story.tension: The sources date the take-off to the end of the civil war, with fast growth from 1993. In the data, income per person still swung hard until 1997, falling 3.8 percent in 1995, so the steady climb only starts in 1998. Since 2016 the sources describe slow economic growth, while income per person has shrunk by 0.4 percent a year, because output has not kept pace with the population.
